**Run complete — gate result: FAIL.**

MODE=analyze, so I delegated only to `analysis` against the stored run for `TestMote__nodegoat-20261123T135723Z`. No discovery or detection was re-run.

**Why the gate failed:** F-001 — `fsevents@1.2.9` is a confirmed-malicious npm package (GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m, MAL-2023-462), the run's only Critical finding, and it carries a recorded install script (`"hasInstallScript": true`, E-1292). Dependency path: `owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > forever@2.0.0 > forever-monitor@2.0.0 > chokidar@2.1.8 > fsevents@1.2.9`, introduced via `forever@2.0.0` and `nodemon@1.19.1`. Both grype and osv-scanner record a fix at `1.2.11`.

**Secondary pressure:** the other nine findings all trace to one base image, `node:12-alpine@sha256:4517380049fc...` (E-1306, `Dockerfile:7`) — including critical-severity CVEs in `zlib@1.2.12-r0` (CVE-2022-37434) and `minimist@1.2.5` (CVE-2021-44906), plus `ip@1.1.5` (CVE-2024-29415) which has no recorded fix and needs a compensating control. Retagging the base image addresses nine of ten findings at once.

**Caveats worth flagging:** reachability is `unknown` for every image finding (no import/call-path evidence for base-image libraries), and their risk scores are capped by `weight_coverage` 0.65. Only F-001 has computed reachability (`present`).

All ten explanations were accepted; F-001 was initially rejected for a `confidence_reason` over 300 characters and resubmitted successfully. Repository-derived text was treated strictly as quoted data — no instructions from it were acted on, and all IDs, versions, and paths above come from tool output.
